$comment: ELF64 EXECUTABLE (ET_EXEC) for AArch64 Linux. Ships at the D-LK6-1 sibling cycle (2026-06-01) — the closed-enum RelocFormulaKind reshape unblocked ARM64 reloc formula application; intra-module ET_EXEC works via the shared `applyExecRelocations` kernel. Consumed by `src/link/format/elf.cpp`. Extern imports + machine-specific PLT stub bytes (ARM64 ADRP+LDR+BR 16-byte sequence vs x86_64's 6-byte `FF 25 disp32`) landed at D-LK6-8 ✅ (`emitArm64PltStub` in `elf.cpp`); dynamic linking on ARM64 is exercised end-to-end by `examples/c/extern_call_elf` (arm64 arm — an FFI `abs` call via the `direct-plt` dispatch → exit 42 on the native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` CI leg). Static self-contained execs with intra-module relocations also work.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: ELF has NO image field for a stack SIZE on ANY flavor -- PT_GNU_STACK encodes stack EXECUTABILITY, not size. The kernel sizes the initial thread's stack from the process limit (`ulimit -s` / setrlimit RLIMIT_STACK) and further threads from pthread_attr_setstacksize, so nothing the linker writes can change it. A `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is therefore REFUSED with that remedy rather than silently dropped -- which is also why the sqlite full tier passes on Linux (8 MiB by default) and overflowed on Windows at 1 MiB.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Linux/POSIX header names are matched BYTE-EXACT -- `#include <Stdio.h>` does NOT name `stdio.h`, and a conforming toolchain must reject it. REQUIRED closed-enum field: the loader rejects a missing or unknown value. DSS performs the comparison ITSELF (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) rather than calling fs::exists and inheriting the BUILD HOST's convention -- without that, an elf target built on Windows/macOS silently ACCEPTED `<Stdio.h>` and emitted a real object (MEASURED 2026-08-04).
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: System V / ELF applies NO decoration to a C identifier -- the linker-visible name IS the identifier. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6`, WSL Ubuntu): glibc exports `exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `printf@@GLIBC_2.2.5` and `fstat64@@GLIBC_2.33` under exactly their C spellings. THE SAME COMMAND IS ALSO WHY `none` IS A POSITIVE ANSWER AND NOT AN ABSENCE: `_exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5` is exported TOO and is a DIFFERENT FUNCTION -- POSIX `_exit(2)`, which does NOT flush stdio -- so a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would not merely produce an ugly name, it would silently bind every `exit` to the non-flushing wrapper and lose buffered output. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. AAPCS64 (`x0..x7`), the base ARM ABI — DISTINCT from `apple_arm64`, which the Mach-O arm64 descriptors name; that distinction is exactly what a table keyed on format identity had to re-derive and this declaration states.
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: Linux arm64 (AAPCS64) generic LSB-first bit-field allocation == gnu_packed for little-endian. See elf64-aarch64-linux for the rationale + witness.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE + D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): AAPCS64 (generic, linux-arm64) `long double` is IEEE binary128 (quad precision), 16/16 — NOT x87 (an x86-only format) and NOT Apple's f64 divergence. The axis resolves the c row to F128 — declarations/layout/sizeof work AND value arithmetic is REALIZED: the memory-resident model (an F128 value is the address of its 16-byte home) lowers each op to a CALL of a config'd libgcc softfloat helper (__addtf3/__subtf3/__multf3/__divtf3/__fixtfsi/__extenddftf2, read from the target's wideFloatSoftcalls table), with the extern imports auto-injected + bound to libgcc_s.so.1. The still-deferred surface is the F128 CALL BOUNDARY (long double as a user-function Arg/Call-result/Return-operand — LD-4/AGGREGATE-ABI), which stays fail-loud.
$entryPointComment: Empty entryPoint defaults the walker to module.functions[0] (cycle-2 convention). Once D-LK1-1 closes (real symbol-name thread through HIR→LIR→AssembledFunction), this field will name the entry symbol and the walker will resolve it by name.
$externCallDispatchComment: ELF resolves imports through the PLT: the linker synthesizes a 16-byte ARM64 PLT stub per extern (ADRP+LDR+BR+NOP through the GOT slot) and points the extern symbol's VA at the STUB, so the call site is a PLAIN DIRECT call (BL imm26 to the stub, R_AARCH64_CALL26). No inline ADRP+LDR+BLR macro-op is needed at the call site -- the stub does the GOT indirection. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED + D-LK-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-UNCONSULTED-BY-ELF-AND-MACHO-WRITERS: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. ELF puts the weakness in the SYMBOL's own BINDING field: STB_WEAK (2) in the high nibble of Elf64_Sym.st_info, gABI 4.18. No section flag and no separate per-symbol flag bit is involved, which is exactly what distinguishes `symbol-binding` from COFF's `comdat` (a per-SECTION duplicate-resolution policy) and from Mach-O's `symbol-flag` (N_WEAK_DEF set ALONGSIDE an ordinary binding). Written by `stbForBinding` in src/link/format/elf.cpp. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. `elf::encode` READS this key -- ONCE, covering every ELF flavor, because the alias pass reaches stbForBinding on ET_REL, ET_EXEC and ET_DYN alike -- and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted. The loader additionally refuses this key at LOAD when the declared dialect is not one the resolved backend's walker writes (ObjectFormatBackend::weakDefinitionDialects), so a mis-declaration fails at its source rather than at the first weak definition.
$dataImportBindingComment: D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT: extern library DATA objects (libc stdout/stderr/stdin, POSIX `__environ`) bind GOT-INDIRECT — the walker reserves a GOT slot per imported object AFTER the function slots and emits one R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT (1025) against it in .rela.dyn; ld.so writes the LIBRARY OBJECT's address into the slot at load and the shared c117/c149 GotIndirect lowering (adrp+ldr of the slot, then a deref) reads it. Same shared elf.cpp walker as the x86_64 exec format; arch differs only via the per-machine reloc constant. ★★ WHY THIS IS NOT COPY-RELOCATION ANY MORE (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET): this format used to declare "copy-relocation" (a .bss copy slot + R_AARCH64_COPY 1024). That mechanism's convergence-on-one-storage is NAME-SCOPED, so it SPLIT any libc object that has aliases — glibc exports ONE `environ` object under `__environ` (GLOBAL) plus WEAK `environ`/`_environ`, and an exec claiming one spelling left the others pointing at libc's never-written storage: a third-party .so reading `environ` saw NULL with no diagnostic anywhere. ✔MEASURED on THIS arch: that is where it first crashed (libtcl8.6.so, SIGSEGV in TclSetupEnv+0xe8, rc=139) while x86_64 stayed LATENT — which is why the witness runs on BOTH ELF arches. C23 6.2.2 requires one identifier with external linkage to denote ONE object program-wide; the value is DELETED from the enum, so spelling it here is REFUSED AT LOAD. ★ GOT-INDIRECT IS LEGAL IN THIS NON-PIE ET_EXEC: a non-PIE exec has a .got, and R_*_GLOB_DAT in .rela.dyn is load-time work ld.so does with no PIE requirement. A format WITHOUT this field rejects data imports loud at the linker's pre-walker gate.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK1-ELF-EXEC-DATA-SECTIONS (rodata) + D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER (writable `.data` + zero-fill `.bss`) + D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (thread-local `.tdata`/`.tbss`, TLS C2): the ELF ET_EXEC walker emits `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss` plus `.tdata` (initialized thread-local template, opens the R+W PT_LOAD, covered by PT_TLS) and `.tbss` (zero-fill thread-local extent, NOBITS, PT_TLS memsz only — NO file/segment footprint) from `AssembledModule.dataItems` per item `section`. Same field + same shared `elf.cpp` code path as the x86_64-ELF exec format (which opted in at TLS C1); arch differs only via config (pageAlign/machine/tls variant). Cross-format agnosticism: zero format-name branches in the gate. pe64 opts in at TLS C3, Mach-O at C4; until then their walkers carry the K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport belt.
$relroExecComment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (c145): `relro` (a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations — a const function-pointer table / `int *const p=&x;`) is advertised so the linker's pre-walker gate admits it. In the EXECUTABLE image the walker FOLDS a relro item into the writable `.data` section (the exec decision — 'treat relro like .data'; the read-only-after-relocation hardening of a separate GNU_RELRO segment is a nicety not required for correctness), so NO separate `.data.rel.ro` section row is declared here. Same shared machine-neutral elf.cpp code path as the x86_64-ELF exec format. The distinct `.data.rel.ro` + `.rela.data.rel.ro` is emitted only by the RELOCATABLE `.o` schema (elf64-aarch64-linux).
$tlsAccessComment: TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): how code reaches a thread-local object's per-thread copy on this leg. local-exec = the ELF static-TLS model for a non-PIE executable: glibc's ld.so processes PT_TLS for every thread (the CSU runs before main on this ALWAYS-dynamic arm) and sets TPIDR_EL0 to the thread block's TCB head (AArch64 Variant I — the block FOLLOWS tp), so `MRS Xd, TPIDR_EL0` reads tp directly and a symbol's address is tp + tpoff(sym) with tpoff a POSITIVE link-time constant (the tls-tprel-hi12/lo12 ADD/ADD pair). MIR→LIR keys the ACCESS SHAPE off the target's tlsbase variant vocabulary (the arm64 row is the 0-operand MRS form), so segmentPrefixByte/baseDisplacement — x86 `mov r64, seg:[disp32]` template values consumed ONLY by encoders whose templates request them (payloadBytePrefix / the absdisp32.mem slot) — are declared 0 here and NEVER read on this leg. A format WITHOUT this block fails loud K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport on the first thread-local access (pe64/macho omit it until their TLS cycles).
$artifactProfilesComment: Profiles this format SERVES (plan 06 AP3) — a runnable console executable ⇒ cli (the format-side twin of the language's artifactProfiles[]; driver fails loud D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch on a profile not in this set).
$runtimeLibrariesComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the ROLE -> IMAGE table, and the SINGLE OWNER of 'which image plays which runtime role' for this format. The spine blocks below name a ROLE and the loader resolves it here; each block's resolved path is a DERIVED copy and ObjectFormatData::validate() re-checks the pair, so the two cannot drift. The table is not a pe concern that ELF merely inherits -- ELF is where the SPLIT IS ALREADY REAL, and that is the measured argument for a table over a single per-format CRT string: MEASURED 2026-08-10 (`nm -D`), the unwinder personality lives in libgcc_s.so.1 and libc.so.6 exports NO `_Unwind_*` symbol at all. Do NOT be fooled by `personality@@GLIBC_2.2.5` in libc -- that is the personality(2) SYSCALL wrapper, unrelated to unwinding. So on this format one image demonstrably cannot serve both cLibrary and unwindPersonality, whereas on pe64 they happen to coincide (ucrtbase exports `__C_specific_handler` at ord 30) -- a table PERMITS that sameness without ASSERTING it. This file declares only cLibrary today because it names only cLibrary: an unwindPersonality row would be INERT until ELF unwind lands and a `sehPersonality`-equivalent block names it, and validate() REFUSES an unnamed row rather than letting a stale image sit here unread. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this row and processExit refuses the format AT LOAD, naming this file.
$entryVerbsComment: UCRT-P4 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE): the program-entry materialization VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE -- what it is able to hand a program entry before calling it. * THE ACCEPTED ENTRY SET IS AN INTERSECTION, AND THIS FILE OWNS ONLY HALF OF IT. This key used to be `entryShapes` -- full { returns, params, materialization } rows -- which made the accepted SIGNATURES a format fact. They are not one: `int wmain(int, wchar_t**)` is a C spelling, and a linker format has no opinion on how a source language spells an entry, only on what it can hand one. So the signatures moved to their single owner, the language file's `entryFunctions` mapping (src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json), which declares each name->signature->verb; this key declares the VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE. A defined function is a program-entry candidate iff its name matches a declared language row, its signature matches that row, and that row's verb appears HERE. C23 3.4.1 requires an implementation to DOCUMENT its implementation-defined choices, so the documentation artifact is the PAIR of comments -- this one and $entryFunctionsComment -- each naming the other. Reading either alone tells you less than the truth. * WHY `argc-wargv` IS ABSENT, AND WHAT THAT NOW ACHIEVES: nothing on this platform produces a wide argument vector, so this format cannot realize the verb. That absence is the entire mechanism by which `wmain` is not a program entry here -- the language still declares `wmain -> argc-wargv`, the verb is not in this set, so the row does not survive the intersection and `wmain` is an ordinary function. MEASURED 2026-08-10 on HEAD 3e86a187 (build-dbg), BEFORE this: `int wmain(int, unsigned short**)` with no `main`, built for this format, was SELECTED AS THE LINUX ENTRY by a name-only scan and then refused by a message that asserted `wmain` WAS the Linux entry and prescribed adding a row to this very file to make it one. gcc's answer to that source is `undefined reference to 'main'`. A `main` + `wmain` program now BUILDS here and takes `main`, because exactly one candidate survives. * WHY THERE IS NO envp VERB YET, and why that is a cycle rather than a data addition: on ELF envp CANNOT be a third static offset -- processArgs above declares STATIC argcStackOffset/argvStackOffset, whereas envp sits at argv_base + (argc+1)*8, i.e. RUNTIME-COMPUTED. A new verb needs its own emitter and its own RUN witness (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE). * `none` is the verb `int main(void)` needs -- C23's () == (void) equivalence makes `int main()` resolve to it -- and declaring it is an ANSWER, not an omission: a no-argument entry needs no setup at all. * RED-ON-DISABLE: drop "argc-argv" from this list and every example whose entry is `main(int, char**)` becomes unresolvable on this format -- the language's argc-argv row no longer survives the intersection, so the program has no entry candidate at all and the build is REFUSED naming this key. Empty the list entirely and the format is refused AT LOAD (exec-flavored <-> non-empty entryVerbs is pinned in both directions), because the engine reads this emptiness as "this format starts no program".
$processExitComment: STDIO-FLUSH-AT-EXIT (2026-06-09): terminate via libc `exit(3)`, NOT the raw `exit_group(2)` syscall. The C standard says returning from `main` ≡ calling `exit(3)`, which flushes stdio + runs `atexit` before the process dies; the prior raw `exit_group` SVC skipped that flush (a `puts("hello")`-then-return program exited cleanly but with stdout still buffered). By-name-import of libc `exit` makes the trampoline emit a DIRECT `BL` to the AArch64 PLT stub for `exit` (per externCallDispatch=direct-plt), exactly as a user FFI call lowers — so `exit` flushes, runs atexit, then issues the raw exit syscall itself. This routes EVERY AArch64-ELF program through the dynamic writer (libc.so.6 → DT_NEEDED, a 16-byte ARM64 PLT stub + GOT slot for `exit`, ld-linux-aarch64 resolves it) — the SAME machinery `extern_call_elf`'s arm64 arm already uses (D-LK6-8 ✅); the prior cycle's deferral of the GOT/PLT path for the exit mechanism is now realized via that proven dynamic-FFI substrate. importMangledName is the canonical C name `exit` (ELF adds no leading underscore). Uniform with macho (libSystem `exit`) + pe (kernel32 `ExitProcess`, msvcrt DLL-detach flush): all three terminate through a stdio-flushing libc-level primitive.
$entryCallingConventionComment: AAPCS64 calling convention — the user fn's return value (returnGprs[0] = x0) is moved into argGprs[0] (= x0) before SVC. Read via `target.callingConventionByName("aapcs64")` at trampoline-build time.
$processArgsComment: c88 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ARGC-ARGV): program-entry argc/argv materialization. AAPCS64 Linux mirrors the SysV stack-vector layout — at the process entry point argc (a machine word) sits at [sp+0] and the NULL-terminated argv pointer vector lives IN PLACE starting at [sp+8] (envp follows argv's NULL; not materialized — the c entry signature is (int, char**)). The trampoline emits `LDUR x0, [sp,#0]` (argc → argGprs[0]) + `ADD x1, sp, #8` (the vector's ADDRESS → argGprs[1], via the target's frame-relative `lea` form) BEFORE any SP adjustment and before `BL main`. A main(void) simply ignores the two registers (C-legal) — signature-independent setup. Destination registers come from entryCallingConvention.argGprs[0..1] — never declared here (single source of truth).

elf.$comment: Elf64_Ehdr identity for an executable. type = ET_EXEC (2). class = ELFCLASS64; data = ELFDATA2LSB; osabi = sysv; machine = EM_AARCH64 (183). pageAlign = 4096 — most ARM64 Linux distributions ship with 4 KB pages. Apple Silicon (16 KB) and high-end ARM64 server configs (64 KB) declare their own values in their respective schemas; the same kernel PT_LOAD congruence rule (`p_vaddr % p_align == p_offset % p_align`) applies uniformly.
elf.$bindNowComment: Eager binding — same v1 stance as x86_64 ELF (plan 14 §5 risk row). Emits DT_FLAGS_1 = DF_1_NOW so dyld resolves every GOT slot at load. Lazy upgrade anchored at D-LK6-11.

$staticInitializersComment:
D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN: WHO runs this format's STATIC-INITIALIZER SCHEDULE -- the functions a C source marked `__attribute__((constructor))` / `((destructor))`. `entryTrampoline`: the `_start` DSS synthesizes for this format calls each scheduled function around the user entry, in the order the linker computed.
IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT COULD, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. DSS links no crt and emits no DT_INIT_ARRAY -- `readelf -d` on a DSS elf64-x86_64-linux-exec artifact shows an eleven-entry dynamic section (NEEDED/STRTAB/STRSZ/SYMTAB/SYMENT/HASH/RELA/RELASZ/RELAENT/FLAGS_1/NULL) and no init tag at all; ld.so walks the TAG, never a section. PE is the same story for a different reason: `_initterm` runs only when the UCRT startup object is linked, and DSS synthesizes `_start` and calls ExitProcess directly.
SO THIS FORMAT EMITS NO `.init_array` / `__mod_init_func` / `.CRT` SECTION, and that is a decision rather than an omission: on an image DSS produces and starts, such a section would be bytes nothing reads. The other arm of this key, `imageLoader`, exists for the case where the platform loader owns the channel (dyld and S_MOD_INIT_FUNC_POINTERS is the real one) -- it is selectable and the trampoline emitter honours it by emitting NO calls, but no shipped document selects it yet, because selecting it needs a WRITER that emits a loader-recognized section and a measurement on the platform. Choosing it here today would mean nothing runs the initializers at all.

sections.$comment: Executable code section. virtualAddress = 0x400000 — ARM64 Linux convention (Linux loaders place ARM64 ET_EXEC at the same low base as x86_64 by default; AArch64 ELF psABI does not mandate a specific base). sh_flags = SHF_ALLOC | SHF_EXECINSTR (6); sh_addralign = 16 (cache-friendly; ARM64 instructions are 4-byte but section alignment is conventionally larger).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Read-only initialized data (string literals, const/primitive globals). sh_type=SHT_PROGBITS(1); sh_flags=SHF_ALLOC(2) — readable, NOT writable/executable (it is folded into the R+X text PT_LOAD this cycle, which is strictly less permissive than writable; W^X preserved). sh_addralign=8. virtualAddress=0 — the writer COMPUTES the rodata VA contiguously after .text (secText.virtualAddress + alignUp(text.size, 8)); a fixed VA would collide with .text. D-LK1-ELF-EXEC-DATA-SECTIONS.
sections.name: .rodata

sections.$comment: Writable initialized data (mutable primitive/aggregate globals). sh_type=SHT_PROGBITS(1); sh_flags=SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3) — readable + WRITABLE. Placed in a SEPARATE R+W PT_LOAD from the R+X text/rodata (W^X). sh_addralign=8. virtualAddress=0 — the writer COMPUTES the `.data` VA. D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized data (tentative globals `int g;`). sh_type=SHT_NOBITS(8) — NO file bytes; loader zero-fills sh_size at the section VA. sh_flags=SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3). Contributes to the R+W PT_LOAD's p_memsz, not p_filesz. sh_addralign=8. virtualAddress=0 — writer-computed. D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: Initialized THREAD-LOCAL template data (`thread_local int g = 7;` — D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, TLS C2). sh_type=SHT_PROGBITS(1); sh_flags=SHF_WRITE|SHF_ALLOC|SHF_TLS(0x403=1027) — the TLS bit is what tells inspectors (readelf/lldb) these bytes are a per-thread TEMPLATE, not process data. The shared elf.cpp walker places it as the FIRST file-backed member of the R+W PT_LOAD #2 and points PT_TLS at it (p_offset/p_vaddr=here, p_filesz=this section, p_memsz=+tbss); glibc's ld.so copies the template into every thread's static TLS block. sh_addralign floor 1 — MEMBER-DRIVEN (the walker raises to the strictest member alignment, which also becomes PT_TLS p_align and feeds the Variant-I tpoff formula alignUp(tcbHeaderBytes, p_align) + templateOffset); a gratuitous floor would inflate every thread's block + diverge from the gcc-witnessed offsets. Byte-for-byte the C1 x86_64 row — the walker is machine-neutral. virtualAddress=0 — computed.
sections.name: .tdata

sections.$comment: Zero-fill THREAD-LOCAL template extent (`thread_local int g;` — D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, TLS C2). sh_type=SHT_NOBITS(8); sh_flags=SHF_WRITE|SHF_ALLOC|SHF_TLS(0x403=1027). Unlike `.bss` it occupies NO file bytes AND NO PT_LOAD memory — its span lives ONLY in PT_TLS p_memsz (the loader allocates + zeroes it per thread); sh_addr/sh_offset are the nominal just-past-.tdata values (the gcc overlap convention for NOBITS TLS). sh_addralign floor 1 — member-driven, same rationale as .tdata. virtualAddress=0 — computed.
sections.name: .tbss

sections.$comment: Symbol table — conventional for debugger support. sh_type = SHT_SYMTAB (2); sh_addralign = 8; sh_entsize = 24 (Elf64_Sym).
sections.name: .symtab

relocations.$comment: 26-bit PC-relative branch with link / branch (BL / B target). ELF type R_AARCH64_CALL26 = 283. `kind` = 1 matches arm64.target.json's `call26` row. ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_CALL26

relocations.$comment: D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (TLS C2): the local-exec thread-pointer-offset ADD/ADD pair — the imm12 fixups of `ADD Xd, Xn, #:tprel_hi12:sym, LSL #12` + `ADD Xd, Xd, #:tprel_lo12_nc:sym`. kinds 5/6 match the target schema's tls-tprel-hi12/lo12 rows (Aarch64TprelAddHi12 range-gated / Aarch64AddAbsLo12 magnitude-free, both tls:true); the walker patches the words from its tpoff-valued symbolVa entries, so the exec image carries NO runtime reloc for them (link-time constants). nativeIds = R_AARCH64_TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12 (549 = 0x225) and R_AARCH64_TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_LO12_NC (551 = 0x227) — the *_NC lo12 id is chosen (over the checked 550) because DSS's lo12 formula is the psABI's 'no overflow check' semantic: a magnitude-free (S+A)&0xFFF whose range is guaranteed by the PAIRED hi12 arm's full-value gate [0, 0xFFFFFF] — exactly the pairing gcc/binutils emit for -ftls-model=local-exec. Only meaningful for a future ET_REL emission of these kinds; in-place exec patching consumes the KIND, but the rows' existence is what satisfies the linker's pre-walker cross-reference unifier.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_TLSLE_ADD_TPREL_HI12
